rv.q: Sarah Snook triumphs in this game-changing piece of theatre
And this is a virtuoso performance in an astonishing piece of theatre.
But as an evening it's an astonishing feat, and Snook magics Wilde's lurid yarn into high-definition life.
Snook...embodies them all with absolute and unflagging conviction
This is raw, human misery, only heightened by the artifice that surrounds it.
Snook is an absolute marvel. Is there anything she can't do?
Kip Williams' version of this dark, queer and sultry novel is not just a one-woman show, but a multi-media spectacular that is nothing short of extraordinary.
The technical sophistication grows and grows, often with high-level wit creating a wicked sense of camp mirroring the themes of the novel.
Her timing is perfect; she has to perform in real time and react to pre-recorded footage, all the while jumping between the role of narrator and every character.
This 'Picture of Dorian Gray' is, on its own terms, a triumph.
This show is a lightweight pastiche, like a French & Saunders spoof, but it lacks the substance for a whole evening's entertainment.

cn.t: Critics praise Sarah Snook's virtuosic performance embodying every character with conviction, though some question whether the production's technical wizardry overshadows the story itself.
